title: Settlements Accounting Basis: the Sum Put Back on a Deductible Recovery
content:
A deductible recovery taken from a host's Keyturn Host Payout Account is put right against what the protection enrolment behind it bears, because the recovery is only ever the host's own share of a settled loss and never more.

## The quantities, in order

1. **The recoveries counted.** The deductible recoveries booked to the account in the month up to the day the correction is worked out, taken as a positive sum.
2. **The appraised sum of the loss.** The appraisal recorded on the most recent appraisal made under the enrolment, rounded half to even to two decimal places.
3. **The deductible the host carries.** The appraised sum of the loss taken at the standard deductible share of 20 percent, rounded half to even to two decimal places.
4. **What is given back.** Nothing of the deductible the host carries is given back; the share given back stands at 0 percent, so the part given back is nothing at all.
5. **The deductible payable.** The deductible the host carries, less whatever of it is given back, rounded half to even to two decimal places.
6. **The sum over-recovered.** The recoveries counted less that deductible payable, rounded half to even to two decimal places.
7. **The part put back at once.** A fifth of the sum over-recovered, that is 20 percent of it, rounded half to even to two decimal places; the rest follows when the claim that produced the recovery is settled.
8. **The correcting entry.** The entry books the share of the sum over-recovered that is put back, rounded half to even to two decimal places, and never less than nothing.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

Take a hypothetical account on which the deductible recoveries booked in the month up to the day come to 1000.00 USD, and a hypothetical enrolment whose most recent appraisal was recorded at 4000.00 USD.

- The appraised sum of the loss is 4000.00 USD.
- The deductible the host carries is that sum at 20 percent, which is 800.00 USD.
- Nothing is given back, so the deductible payable is 800.00 USD.
- The sum over-recovered is 1000.00 USD less 800.00 USD, which is 200.00 USD.
- A fifth of that is 40.00 USD, and 40.00 USD is what the correcting entry books.

Where the recoveries counted come to less than the deductible payable, the sum over-recovered falls below nothing and the entry books nothing at all rather than a negative figure: on hypothetical recoveries of 600.00 USD against the same deductible payable of 800.00 USD, the figure the entry books is 0.00 USD.
